pr_title: Correctly set the organization num repos
pr_body:
Correctly set the organization num repos to the number of
accessible repos for the user

- In writing the test for this I have noticed that the API for create Org is broken in several places due to the incorrect use of :orgname when it should be :org. This PR therefore contains fixes for these.

Fix #11194
Fix #11331

Signed-off-by: Andrew Thornton <art27@cantab.net>
pr_comments:
@zeripath can we add a test for OrgRepoNum somewhere?
Presumably there is something in `models/org_test.go` but the tests are totally opaque. There's not really anything appropriate in `integrations` - we'd literally have to create a declarative test format that would create organizations, teams, repositories, set members etc.

---

OK I've added the test. I've done it in the declarative style with reusable component tests.
Organisations disapiear on "My Organizations" if they have no repo
![Bildschirmfoto zu 2020-05-11 03-20-43](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/24977596/81515926-7180b980-9336-11ea-88c7-00b04f1113fc.png)
@6543 presumably this is going to need a `LEFT` when joining the repository table.

issue_context.body:
- Gitea version (or commit ref): 1.11.4
- Git version: doesnt matter
- Operating system: Ubuntu 18.04
- Database (use `[x]`):
  - [ ] PostgreSQL
  - [x] MySQL
  - [ ] MSSQL
  - [ ] SQLite
- Can you reproduce the bug at https://try.gitea.io:
  - [ ] Yes (provide example URL)
  - [ ] No
  - [x] Not relevant
- Log gist:

## Description

User sees all public and private repository count in Dashboard (under organizations tab), even if private repos are outside of team and user has no rights. When opening company profile then repositories that are shown are correct. User should see only public and team repositories count and not private ones that he has no access to it.


## Screenshots

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/195263/80146772-06f01f80-85bb-11ea-9f1f-a11759227241.png)

review_comments: do you forgot to remove debugging code?
ah I got it, this way you can avoid the x.IN(select ID by ... query).Get/Del construct ...
Since there is no insert/update/delete operations here, a transation is unnecessary. If you still want that, you should add `defer sess.Close()`.
